formulation.evidence: The item defines both branches, the reduced length-flow Killing generator and reference normalization, the exponential test coordinate, the massless proper-time smearing, the energy-frequency conversions, coupling units, and the complete two-state rate equation.

scope.evidence: The statement limits itself to the two selected effective models, says the exponential ray map is an adopted input, excludes a point-field restriction, and makes no general KMS, Hawking, detector-probability, or empirical claim.

sources.evidence: Three independent full-text treatments were inspected: Preskill §§4.3 and 4.7, Wald §3, and Crispino–Higuchi–Matsas §III.A.1–2. Their ideal point-detector/KMS material is recorded as context with its limitations; each URL has a fetch stamp.

non_derivation.evidence: The item is explicitly an adopted model with no Proof section, no invented observation, no measured temperature, and no claim that its rates follow as exact QFT transition probabilities.

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as defined in [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the mathematical context for the tested-current, Fourier and temporally smeared field constructions used below.

Use the length-coordinate, unit, and reference conventions of [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. Adopt two distinct model branches.

**Reduced exponential-current branch.** Choose a constant $\kappa>0$ in inverse metres and a smooth Killing field $\xi$ on a declared domain in the TGR framework. The real parameter $u$, measured in metres, is the selected flow parameter for $\xi$; the reference event and normalization of this flow are fixed as part of the model. Set the exponential coordinate $U_\kappa(u)=-\kappa^{-1}e^{-\kappa u}$. Adopt the positive-chiral-current vacuum and tested current $j_\kappa$ constructed in [[lem-tgr-exponential-current]]. Its mathematical two-point covariance is the tested boundary $C_\kappa$ there; use its angular-frequency spectrum $S_\kappa$ and detailed-balance convention exactly as stated in [[lem-tgr-thermal-contour-spectrum]]. The exponential ray map and the choice of $\kappa$ are model inputs. If $\xi$ and $\kappa$ are identified with a generator and geometric surface gravity of a particular horizon, that identification is an additional physical assumption; no collapse geometry, four-dimensional horizon restriction, scattering factor, or backreaction is derived here.

**Massless acceleration branch.** Adopt the massless scalar and Minkowski vacuum of [[post-qft-free-field-model]]. Use the actually defined temporal smearing along the smooth proper-time hyperbola and its tested covariance from [[lem-tgr-timelike-scalar-acceleration]]. The curve-smeared field is not a sharp-point field. Its accelerated spectrum and finite-switch coefficient are used only with the conditional hypotheses recorded in that lemma and in [[lem-tgr-spectral-thermometer]].

For either branch, select an energy gap $E>0$ joules and define a two-state, continuous-time rate model with ground state $g$, excited state $e$, and proper-time coordinate $t\ge0$ measured in seconds. In the reduced branch let $\gamma_{\rm red}>0$ have units metres per second and set $r_\uparrow=\gamma_{\rm red}S_\kappa(E/(\hbar c))$ and $r_\downarrow=\gamma_{\rm red}S_\kappa(-E/(\hbar c))$. In the acceleration branch let $\gamma_{\rm acc}>0$ have units square metres per square second and set $r_\uparrow=\gamma_{\rm acc}S_a(E/\hbar)$ and $r_\downarrow=\gamma_{\rm acc}S_a(-E/\hbar)$. Here $c>0$ is metres per second, $\hbar>0$ is joule-seconds, and the frequency arguments have units inverse metres and inverse seconds, respectively. These choices make both rates inverse seconds. The adopted population $p(t)$ of state $e$ is the solution of $p'(t)=r_\uparrow(1-p(t))-r_\downarrow p(t)$ with supplied $p(0)\in[0,1]$. This differential equation is the entire effective two-state model; the rates are adopted inputs, not exact QFT transition probabilities.

Only when a selected construction also supplies a density state and a normalized finite measurement instrument may an outcome be read using [[post-qft-constructed-model-and-measurement]]. No such state, instrument, detector apparatus, or observed outcome is supplied here. The postulate asserts no general thermalization, exact all-order transition probability, KMS state, or experimental temperature reading.

On a nonempty connected open set $O$ in the smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of [[def-tgr-framework-units]], select one smooth future timelike Killing field $\xi$ and one smooth scalar $T:O\to(0,\infty)$ in kelvins. Its dimensionless lapse and selected observer congruence are

$$N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0,\qquad u:=\xi/N_\xi.$$

Thus $g(u,u)=-1$ and the physical four-velocity is $cu$ in the length-coordinate convention $x^0=ct$. A reference normalization of $\xi$ is part of the selected model. The local temperature $T$ is assigned to this comoving observer congruence; it is not a coordinate temperature or a value assigned to every observer.

Adopt the inverse-temperature vector

$$\beta:=\frac{u}{k_BT},$$

where $k_B>0$ is Boltzmann's constant in joules per kelvin, and assume that this field is Killing on $O$. In this item, a selected stationary thermal equilibrium means precisely this adopted bath, observer congruence, positive proper-temperature field, and Killing condition on $\beta$. The field $N_\xi T$ is not assumed constant here; its constancy is the conclusion of [[pthm-tgr-tolman-ehrenfest]].

This is a model assumption, not a statement that every stationary geometry admits a thermal state or that every material realizes this bath. It asserts no complete Killing flow, KMS state, trace-class stress exponential, collision or thermalization law, Hawking or Unruh temperature, or empirical thermometer reading.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $A,b>0$, put $\beta=\pi/b$ and $L=A/b^2$, and define the analytic kernel
$$C(z)=-A\operatorname{csch}^2(bz),\qquad \operatorname{csch}w=1/\sinh w.$$
Use the angular-frequency convention
$$\widehat\varphi(\omega)=\int_{\mathbb R}\varphi(s)e^{-i\omega s}\,ds,\qquad \varphi(s)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}\widehat\varphi(\omega)e^{i\omega s}\,d\omega$$
for Schwartz functions $\varphi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$, where Schwartz space has seminorms $\sup_s|s^m\varphi^{(n)}(s)|$ and a tempered distribution is a continuous complex-linear functional on that space. Define its Fourier transform by the bilinear pairing $\langle\widehat T,\varphi\rangle=\langle T,\widehat\varphi\rangle$; test functions are not conjugated.

For $0<\epsilon<\beta$, $C_\epsilon(s)=C(s-i\epsilon)$ is a smooth $L^1$ function. These regularizations have a limit $C_{A,b}\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R)$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$, denoted $-A\operatorname{csch}^2(b(s-i0))$. The kernel is holomorphic on $-\beta<\operatorname{Im}z<0$, has period $i\beta$, and its tested boundary values obey
$$C(s-i\beta+i0)=C(-s-i0).$$
The Fourier transform of $C_{A,b}$ is the continuous nonnegative function
$$S_{A,b}(\omega)=\frac{2\pi(A/b^2)\omega}{e^{\pi\omega/b}-1},\qquad S_{A,b}(0)=\frac{2\pi L}{\beta}=\frac{2A}{b}.$$
In particular $S_{A,b}(-\omega)=e^{\beta\omega}S_{A,b}(\omega)$ for $\omega>0$. The zero-frequency value is the removable limit, and the boundary and Fourier assertions are distributional, not pointwise integrals at a double pole.

If the coordinate has a specified unit, $s,z,\beta,\epsilon$ have that unit and $b,\omega$ its reciprocal. If $A$ has covariance units, $L$ has those units times the square of the coordinate unit and $S_{A,b}$ has those units times the coordinate unit.

In particular, for $\kappa>0$ in inverse length, take $A=\kappa^2/(16\pi)$ and $b=\kappa/2$. Then $L=1/(4\pi)$, $\beta=2\pi/\kappa$, and $C_{A,b}$ is precisely the tested chiral covariance $C_\kappa$ of [[lem-tgr-exponential-current]]. Its spectrum and detailed balance are
$$S_\kappa(\omega)=\frac{\omega}{2(e^{2\pi\omega/\kappa}-1)},\qquad S_\kappa(0)=\frac{\kappa}{4\pi},\qquad S_\kappa(-\omega)=e^{2\pi\omega/\kappa}S_\kappa(\omega)\quad(\omega>0).$$
Here $C_\kappa$ has units of inverse length squared and $S_\kappa$ inverse length. This is a two-point strip and detailed-balance statement, including the specified chiral current as a specialization. It does not assert a norm-continuous $C^*$-algebra KMS dynamics or an exact detector transition probability.

Use a smooth, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with its metric-selected Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$, as defined in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. A chart is a smooth coordinate map; an observer congruence is a smooth future-directed unit timelike vector field $u$ with $g(u,u)=-1$; its integral curves, an adapted chart, and a tetrad field are distinct objects. The exact regularity and rest-space conventions of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and the chart/congruence distinction of [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]] apply. An orthogonal family of rest slices is not available for every congruence.

For physical unit assignments use length coordinates $x^0=ct_{\rm phys}$ and spatial coordinates in metres, where $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. In this convention the metric components, a unit observer $u$, and a length-normalized Killing field $\xi$ are dimensionless. Other coordinate choices transform component units by their coordinate Jacobians. State maps and geometric currents have the types and units in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]: a formal marker density $n$ is $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; entropy density $s$ is $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; a $C^1$ entropy current $S^a$ has components $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; and its physical flux is $cS^a$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Its geometric divergence $\nabla_aS^a$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-4}}$, so $c\nabla_aS^a$ is entropy production per physical volume per second. The symmetric stress tensor $\mathsf T^{ab}$ has components in pascals in length coordinates; it is a tensor, not an observer-independent array of energy densities. The state-function energy density $\varepsilon$ and the observer projection $\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b$ remain distinct unless a material model identifies them.

The constant $c$ supplies the spacetime length/time conversion. In a branch with dynamical Einstein gravity, $G$ is an independent coupling parameter in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$. The Boltzmann constant $k_B$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ and is used when a statistical entropy/temperature calibration is adopted. Planck's constant $h_{\rm P}=2\pi\hbar$ has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$; $\hbar$ is used only in a quantum branch. Under the current SI definition, $c$, $h_{\rm P}$ and $k_B$ have exact defining numerical values; this metrological fact does not make them derived predictions of a thermodynamic or gravitational model. $G$ is experimentally adjusted and carries measurement uncertainty. The roles of these quantities as primitive model inputs are framework-specific. The local energy function, pressure, temperature and chemical potential in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] are derived from the supplied state function; no particle mass or universal equation of state is derived from gravity alone.

For a smooth Killing field $\xi$ on an open domain, meaning $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$ by [[def-gr-killing-field]], restrict attention to a domain where $\xi$ is future timelike and choose a positive normalization at infinity or at a specified wall/observer. Define the lapse $N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and unit observer $u_\xi:=\xi/N_\xi$. For a supplied proper-temperature scalar $T>0$ in kelvins, define the Killing-normalized temperature field $T_\xi:=N_\xi T$. It is not assumed constant; if a separate equilibrium argument proves constancy on its stated domain, denote that value by $T_K$. The finite matter charge and its side-flux convention are those in [[lem-tgr-killing-energy-normalization]] and [[def-tgr-spacelike-current-slab]]; their charge-balance clause retains its explicitly conditional finite-slab hypotheses. This charge is not a general gravitational energy.

Keep covector types separate. A mechanical momentum covector $p_a$ has units $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$; its Killing energy is $E_\xi(p):=-c\,p_a\xi^a$ in joules. An energy-valued covector $\pi_a$ already has units joules and pairs as $E_\xi(\pi):=-\pi_a\xi^a$, without another factor of $c$. An inverse-length wave covector $k_a$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and pairs as $E_\xi(k):=-\hbar c\,k_a\xi^a$. For a specified charged stationary gauge, charge $q$ has coulombs and a potential covector $A_a$ in length coordinates has units $\mathrm{V\,s\,m^{-1}}$; when a global stationary potential is actually defined, $\Phi_\xi:=-cA_a\xi^a$ has volts and $q\Phi_\xi$ has joules. A charged energy or chemical-potential convention requires its stated gauge and reference; no global potential, electrochemical equilibrium, or constancy is asserted here.

When $T_K>0$ is supplied, distinguish the inverse-temperature vector $\beta^a:=u_\xi^a/(k_BT)=\xi^a/(k_BT_K)$, with units $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, from the scalar $\beta_K:=1/(k_BT_K)$, also in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$. For a quantum statistical model, let $\mathcal A$ be a unital complex $C^*$-algebra: an associative complex algebra with nonzero identity $1$, a complete norm satisfying $\|AB\|\leq\|A\|\,\|B\|$, and a conjugate-linear involution $A\mapsto A^*$ satisfying $(A^*)^*=A$, $(AB)^*=B^*A^*$, and $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$. Its elements represent bounded observables. Let $\{\alpha_t:t\in\mathbb R\}$ be bijective complex-linear maps $\alpha_t:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ preserving multiplication and involution, with $\alpha_t(1)=1$, $\alpha_0=\operatorname{id}$, and $\alpha_{s+t}=\alpha_s\circ\alpha_t$; require $t\mapsto\alpha_t(A)$ to be norm-continuous for every $A\in\mathcal A$. A state is a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ with $\omega(1)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\geq0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$. For $b>0$ in the chosen flow-parameter units, define $S_b:=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\leq\operatorname{Im}z\leq b\}$. The state $\omega$ satisfies the KMS condition at width $b$ when for every $A,B\in\mathcal A$ there is a function $F_{A,B}:S_b\to\mathbb C$ with $\sup_{z\in S_b}|F_{A,B}(z)|<\infty$, continuous on $S_b$ and complex-differentiable at every point of its interior, such that

$$F_{A,B}(t)=\omega(A\alpha_t(B)),\qquad F_{A,B}(t+ib)=\omega(\alpha_t(B)A)\quad(t\in\mathbb R).$$

This all-observable boundary-value definition uses no separately declared analytic subalgebra. With the quantum statistical calibration $\beta_K=(k_BT_K)^{-1}$, a physical-time parameter $t$ in seconds has KMS width $b_t=\hbar\beta_K$ seconds. If the flow parameter is length $\lambda=ct$, use the reparameterized group $\widetilde\alpha_\lambda:=\alpha_{\lambda/c}$; its KMS width is $b_\lambda=c\hbar\beta_K$ metres. These are unit and parameter-convention assignments only. This definition introduces no Hilbert-space operator $H_K$ and does not identify the abstract automorphism flow or its strip width with the finite matter charge $H_\xi$ of [[lem-tgr-killing-energy-normalization]]. This item asserts neither the existence of an observable algebra or flow for a given thermodynamic-gravity model nor the existence of a KMS state or equilibrium.

On a specified smooth embedded null hypersurface $\mathcal H\subset M$,
write $i:\mathcal H\hookrightarrow M$ for the inclusion. A generator $\chi$
here is a smooth section of $i^*TM$ with $\chi_p\in T_p\mathcal H$
nonzero and null at each $p\in\mathcal H$. For a smooth tangent field $X$
on $\mathcal H$ and a smooth vector field $V$ along it, define
$\nabla_XV:=(i^*\nabla)_XV$ by [[def-pullback-connection]], applied to the
ambient tangent bundle and its metric-selected connection. The prescription
is independent of frames by
[[thm-pullback-connection-is-well-defined-and-functorial]]. In particular,
$\nabla_\chi\chi$ is a vector field along $\mathcal H$ and needs no chosen
ambient extension. If $\chi$ is the restriction of a smooth ambient field
$\widetilde\chi$, the same theorem gives
$\nabla_\chi\chi=(\nabla_{\widetilde\chi}\widetilde\chi)|_{\mathcal H}$;
thus this convention also covers the supplied ambient Killing generators.
The generator may admit a scalar $\kappa_{\rm geom}$ defined by
$\nabla_\chi\chi=\kappa_{\rm geom}\chi$. When the flow parameter has length units, $\kappa_{\rm geom}$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$; the corresponding acceleration-unit quantity $\kappa_{\rm acc}:=c^2\kappa_{\rm geom}$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. This definition does not assert a horizon exists, that $\kappa$ is constant, or that a temperature law follows. The formula $T_K=\hbar c\kappa_{\rm geom}/(2\pi k_B)$ requires a specified quantum/semiclassical model, and an area-entropy formula requires a separate thermodynamic identification. In particular, equal units do not identify local material entropy, finite statistical entropy, and area entropy, and no generalized second law is asserted here.

Let $O$ and the smooth fields $(g,\nabla,\xi,T,u,N_\xi,\beta)$ be as in
[[def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers]]. Then
$$\beta\text{ is Killing}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N_\xi T=T_K\text{ for a constant }T_K>0.$$
When this holds, $\beta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$, and the Killing congruence has
$$\xi(N_\xi)=0,\qquad a=\nabla\log N_\xi,\qquad \theta=0,\qquad \sigma_{ab}=0.$$
If $\xi$ is replaced by $b\xi$ with a constant $b>0$, then
$N_\xi$ and $T_K$ scale by $b$, while $u$ and $\beta$ are unchanged.

Use the connected stationary thermal carrier of [[post-tgr-stationary-equilibrium]] on $O$. Let $N_\xi=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$, $u=\xi/N_\xi$, and $\beta=u/(k_BT)$ as there, and assume the postulated Killing condition on $\beta$. Then a positive constant $T_K$ exists such that

$N_\xi(x)T(x)=T_K\quad\text{and}\quad \beta=\frac{\xi}{k_BT_K}\qquad(x\in O).$

In the same convention, $\xi(N_\xi)=0$, the observer acceleration satisfies $a=\nabla\log N_\xi$, the expansion and shear vanish, and

$\nabla\log T=-a.$

For any chosen reference event $x_{\rm ref}\in O$, $T_K=N_\xi(x_{\rm ref})T(x_{\rm ref})$. If the reference normalization has $N_\xi(x_{\rm ref})=1$, then $T_K$ is the local temperature at that event. Rescaling $\xi$ by a constant $b>0$ rescales $N_\xi$ and $T_K$ by $b$ while leaving the local scalar $T$ unchanged. The result is a conditional deduction from the selected physical postulate and the stated mathematical supplier; it is not a thermometer law for arbitrary observers or a KMS-existence theorem.

The real exponential function is $C^\infty$, and for every $m\in\mathbb N$,
$$\exp^{(m)}=\exp.$$
In particular $(\exp)'=\exp$.

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ ([[def-continuity-real]], [[def-interval]]) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
([[def-derivative]]). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

**Continuity on the closed interval cannot be dropped.** Differentiability at
every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and
the companion page works the same witness out in full.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim:
Under the Countable Choice assumption [A4], since $E,\hbar,c,\kappa>0$, $
u=E/(\hbar c)>0$. By [F1], both $S_\kappa(
u)$ and $S_\kappa(-
u)$ are positive and their ratio is $S_\kappa(-
u)/S_\kappa(
u)=e^{2\pi
u/\kappa}$. Multiplying by the same $\gamma_{m red}>0$ gives $r_\uparrow,r_\downarrow>0$ and $r_\downarrow/r_\uparrow=e^{2\pi E/(\hbar c\kappa)}$.

Put $R=r_\uparrow+r_\downarrow$ and $p_*=r_\uparrow/R$. Then $0<p_*<1$, and $p(t)=p_*+(p(0)-p_*)e^{-Rt}$ satisfies the adopted equation and the initial condition by [F5]. It is a probability because $p(t)=e^{-Rt}p(0)+(1-e^{-Rt})p_*$ and $0<e^{-Rt}\le1$ for $t\ge0$. For any other differentiable solution, $q(t)=e^{Rt}(p(t)-p_*)$ has zero derivative by the rate equation and [F5]; [F6] makes $q$ constant on every compact time interval, so the displayed solution is unique. Its stationary value is therefore $p_*$.

From $p_*=r_\uparrow/R$ and $1-p_*=r_\downarrow/R$, we have $p_*/(1-p_*)=r_\uparrow/r_\downarrow=e^{-2\pi E/(\hbar c\kappa)}$ by step 1.1. The exponential is strictly increasing by [F5] and [F6], so comparison with the defining Boltzmann ratio gives $E/(k_BT_{\rm red})=2\pi E/(\hbar c\kappa)$. Since $E>0$, solving yields $T_{\rm red}=\hbar c\kappa/(2\pi k_B)$, which has kelvin units.

Under the optional assumptions [A2]–[A3], [F3]–[F4] give $T(x)=T_K/N_\xi(x)$ on $O$. Evaluating at $x_{\rm ref}$ and using $N_\xi(x_{\rm ref})=1$ and [A3] sets $T_K=T_{\rm red}$. Substitution gives $T(x)=T_{\rm red}/N_\xi(x)$. The result is conditional on the separately adopted bath and reference match.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the affine Minkowski
space, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, shell pairing
$p\circ x=p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x$, and massless one-particle space
of [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]]. Thus $x^0,\mathbf x$ have length units,
$\mathbf k$ has inverse-length units, the omitted shell apex $\mathbf k=0$
has measure zero, and
$$d\nu_0(\mathbf k)=\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3 2|\mathbf k|},\qquad \mathcal H_0=L^2(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\},d\nu_0;\mathbb C).$$

seconds, and let $\gamma=(\gamma^0,\boldsymbol\gamma)\in
C^\infty(I,\mathbb R^4)$ satisfy
$$\eta(\dot\gamma(\tau),\dot\gamma(\tau))=-c^2,\qquad \dot\gamma^0(\tau)>|\dot{\boldsymbol\gamma}(\tau)|$$
for all $\tau\in I$, where $c>0$ is in metres per second. This defines a
future-directed timelike curve parametrized by proper seconds. For
$f\in C_c^\infty(I;\mathbb C)$ define its curve-smearing amplitude by
$$K_\gamma f(\mathbf k)=\int_I f(\tau) e^{i(|\mathbf k|\gamma^0(\tau)-\mathbf k\cdot\boldsymbol\gamma(\tau))}\,d\tau.$$
Then $K_\gamma f\in\mathcal H_0$, and on every fixed compact support set the
map $f\mapsto K_\gamma f$ is continuous in the test-function topology. If
$f$ has units metres per second, then $K_\gamma f$ has units metres and its
$\mathcal H_0$ norm is dimensionless. For real $f$, define the actual
finite-particle-domain field
$$\Phi_\gamma(f)=a(K_\gamma f)+a^\dagger(K_\gamma f)$$
using the bosonic Fock space and creation/annihilation conventions of
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. It is symmetric on the finite-particle
domain and has the self-adjoint Segal closure supplied by
[[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]]. Its vacuum covariance on real compact tests is
the well-defined pairing $\langle K_\gamma f,K_\gamma g\rangle_2$. This
construction is an additional temporal smearing of the massless shell; it
does not define a point field or an interaction.

For $a>0$ in metres per second squared, put $\ell=c^2/a$ and define the
uniformly accelerated curve on $I=\mathbb R$ by
$$\gamma_a(\tau)=\bigl(\ell\sinh(a\tau/c),\ell\cosh(a\tau/c),0,0\bigr).$$
It has proper acceleration magnitude $a$. The restriction of the massless
Minkowski-vacuum covariance constructed above is stationary and, in the
distributional boundary-value sense on the real line, is
$$C_a(s)=-\frac{a^2}{16\pi^2c^4}\,\operatorname{csch}^2\!\left(\frac{a(s-i0)}{2c}\right).$$
Here $\operatorname{csch}z=1/\sinh z$, and the displayed expression means
the limit of the smooth damped shell pairings against compact smooth tests;
no product or pullback of point-field distributions is assumed. With the
angular-frequency convention
$$S_a(\nu)=\mathcal F_{-}C_a(\nu),\qquad \mathcal F_{-}C(\nu)=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-i\nu s}C(s)\,ds$$
interpreted distributionally, the local conclusion about the spectrum is conditional on the current
batch-74 draft suppliers [[lem-tgr-thermal-contour-spectrum]] and its
prerequisite [[lem-tgr-exponential-current]]. Their carriers exist in the
batch-74 manifest, but both items are status `draft` and have no Step-1
readiness records. The contour item's actual statement uses a length
coordinate and an inverse-length parameter (renamed from its $\kappa$ to
$\alpha$ here); the proof below uses
$\alpha=a/c^2$ and $u=cs$, for which the covariance obeys
$C_a(s)=\pi^{-1}C_\alpha(cs)$. Under the contour item's exact conditional
Fourier formula and this rescaling,
$$S_a(\nu)=\frac{\nu}{2\pi c^2\bigl(e^{2\pi c\nu/a}-1\bigr)},\qquad S_a(0)=\frac{a}{4\pi^2c^3},\qquad S_a(-\nu)=e^{2\pi c\nu/a}S_a(\nu)\quad(\nu>0).$$
The continuous value at zero is the removable limit. $\nu$ has units
seconds$^{-1}$ and $S_a$ has units seconds per square metre; the spectral
claim remains conditional until both draft suppliers are accepted.

For comparison, on the inertial curve $\gamma_0(\tau)=(c\tau,0,0,0)$ the
same construction gives
$$C_0(s)=-\frac{1}{4\pi^2c^2(s-i0)^2},\qquad S_0(\nu)=\frac{\max(-\nu,0)}{2\pi c^2}.$$
These are mathematical covariance and Fourier-transform statements in the
specified representation. They do not assert a measured spectrum or a
detector transition probability.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the massless accelerated
covariance $C_a$ and its conditional spectrum $S_a$ from
[[lem-tgr-timelike-scalar-acceleration]], with $a>0$ in metres per second
squared, $c>0$ in metres per second, and angular frequency in seconds$^{-1}$.
The conditional detailed-balance input is the actual Statement of the
current batch-74 draft [[lem-tgr-thermal-contour-spectrum]], reproduced in
[L1] below. Its declared prerequisite [[lem-tgr-exponential-current]] is also
a draft, and neither item has Step-1 readiness evidence. The inertial
pair $(C_0,S_0)$ is the unconditioned comparison from
[[lem-tgr-timelike-scalar-acceleration]]. Both spectra are continuous and
globally Lipschitz. The conventions are $S=\mathcal F_-C$ with kernel
$e^{-i\nu s}$ and $C$ paired bilinearly with Schwartz tests.

Let $h\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb R)$ be nonzero, let the switching
duration $\mathsf T>0$ be measured in seconds, and put
$$\widehat h(z)=\int_{\mathbb R}h(u)e^{-izu}\,du,\qquad K_h=\frac{1}{2\pi\|h\|_2^2}\int_{\mathbb R}|z|\,|\widehat h(z)|^2\,dz.$$
For either stationary pair $(C,S)=(C_a,S_a)$ or $(C_0,S_0)$ define the
switched coefficient
$$R_{\mathsf T}^{(C)}(\nu)=\left\langle C(s),e^{-i\nu s} \int_{\mathbb R}h(t/\mathsf T)h((t-s)/\mathsf T)\,dt\right\rangle.$$
Then $K_h<\infty$ and, for every $\nu\in\mathbb R$,
$$R_{\mathsf T}^{(C)}(\nu)=\frac{\mathsf T^2}{2\pi} \int_{\mathbb R}S(\omega)|\widehat h(\mathsf T(\nu-\omega))|^2\,d\omega,$$
so $R_{\mathsf T}^{(C)}(\nu)\ge0$, and
$$\left|\frac{R_{\mathsf T}^{(C)}(\nu)}{\mathsf T\|h\|_2^2}-S(\nu)\right| \le\frac{\operatorname{Lip}(S)K_h}{\mathsf T},\qquad \operatorname{Lip}(S)=\sup_{x\ne y}\frac{|S(x)-S(y)|}{|x-y|}<\infty.$$
This proves the leading switched coefficient limit and its explicit error;
it is not a convergence theorem for an all-order detector transition
probability or an exact infinite-time probability.

There is also the following separately defined two-state continuous-time
Markov model. Choose an energy $E>0$ in joules, $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds,
$k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin, and a coupling $\gamma_d>0$ in square metres
per square second. For the accelerated spectrum set
$$r_+=\gamma_d S_a(E/\hbar),\qquad r_-=\gamma_d S_a(-E/\hbar).$$
These are positive rates in seconds$^{-1}$. Let $p(t)$ be the probability
of the excited state in the two-state chain with ground-to-excited rate
$r_+$ and excited-to-ground rate $r_-$. For $t\ge0$ and any initial probability $p(0)\in[0,1]$, then
$$p(t)=p_*+(p(0)-p_*)e^{-(r_++r_-)t},\qquad p_* =\frac{1}{1+e^{2\pi cE/(a\hbar)}}.$$
If the effective thermometer temperature $T_{\rm eff}>0$ is defined by
$p_*/(1-p_*)=e^{-E/(k_BT_{\rm eff})}$, then
$$T_{\rm eff}=\frac{\hbar a}{2\pi c k_B}.$$
This is an exact result for the specified Markov chain. It is not a weak
coupling or point-detector thermalization theorem.

Use a smooth, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g)$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with its metric-selected Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$, as defined in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. A chart is a smooth coordinate map; an observer congruence is a smooth future-directed unit timelike vector field $u$ with $g(u,u)=-1$; its integral curves, an adapted chart, and a tetrad field are distinct objects. The exact regularity and rest-space conventions of [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and the chart/congruence distinction of [[thm-sr-local-congruence-adapted-charts-and-frobenius]] apply. An orthogonal family of rest slices is not available for every congruence.

For physical unit assignments use length coordinates $x^0=ct_{\rm phys}$ and spatial coordinates in metres, where $c>0$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. In this convention the metric components, a unit observer $u$, and a length-normalized Killing field $\xi$ are dimensionless. Other coordinate choices transform component units by their coordinate Jacobians. State maps and geometric currents have the types and units in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]]: a formal marker density $n$ is $\mathrm{marker\,m^{-3}}$; entropy density $s$ is $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; a $C^1$ entropy current $S^a$ has components $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$; and its physical flux is $cS^a$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. Its geometric divergence $\nabla_aS^a$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-4}}$, so $c\nabla_aS^a$ is entropy production per physical volume per second. The symmetric stress tensor $\mathsf T^{ab}$ has components in pascals in length coordinates; it is a tensor, not an observer-independent array of energy densities. The state-function energy density $\varepsilon$ and the observer projection $\mathsf T^{ab}u_a u_b$ remain distinct unless a material model identifies them.

The constant $c$ supplies the spacetime length/time conversion. In a branch with dynamical Einstein gravity, $G$ is an independent coupling parameter in $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$. The Boltzmann constant $k_B$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ and is used when a statistical entropy/temperature calibration is adopted. Planck's constant $h_{\rm P}=2\pi\hbar$ has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$; $\hbar$ is used only in a quantum branch. Under the current SI definition, $c$, $h_{\rm P}$ and $k_B$ have exact defining numerical values; this metrological fact does not make them derived predictions of a thermodynamic or gravitational model. $G$ is experimentally adjusted and carries measurement uncertainty. The roles of these quantities as primitive model inputs are framework-specific. The local energy function, pressure, temperature and chemical potential in [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] are derived from the supplied state function; no particle mass or universal equation of state is derived from gravity alone.

For a smooth Killing field $\xi$ on an open domain, meaning $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$ by [[def-gr-killing-field]], restrict attention to a domain where $\xi$ is future timelike and choose a positive normalization at infinity or at a specified wall/observer. Define the lapse $N_\xi:=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$ and unit observer $u_\xi:=\xi/N_\xi$. For a supplied proper-temperature scalar $T>0$ in kelvins, define the Killing-normalized temperature field $T_\xi:=N_\xi T$. It is not assumed constant; if a separate equilibrium argument proves constancy on its stated domain, denote that value by $T_K$. The finite matter charge and its side-flux convention are those in [[lem-tgr-killing-energy-normalization]] and [[def-tgr-spacelike-current-slab]]; their charge-balance clause retains its explicitly conditional finite-slab hypotheses. This charge is not a general gravitational energy.

Keep covector types separate. A mechanical momentum covector $p_a$ has units $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$; its Killing energy is $E_\xi(p):=-c\,p_a\xi^a$ in joules. An energy-valued covector $\pi_a$ already has units joules and pairs as $E_\xi(\pi):=-\pi_a\xi^a$, without another factor of $c$. An inverse-length wave covector $k_a$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and pairs as $E_\xi(k):=-\hbar c\,k_a\xi^a$. For a specified charged stationary gauge, charge $q$ has coulombs and a potential covector $A_a$ in length coordinates has units $\mathrm{V\,s\,m^{-1}}$; when a global stationary potential is actually defined, $\Phi_\xi:=-cA_a\xi^a$ has volts and $q\Phi_\xi$ has joules. A charged energy or chemical-potential convention requires its stated gauge and reference; no global potential, electrochemical equilibrium, or constancy is asserted here.

When $T_K>0$ is supplied, distinguish the inverse-temperature vector $\beta^a:=u_\xi^a/(k_BT)=\xi^a/(k_BT_K)$, with units $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, from the scalar $\beta_K:=1/(k_BT_K)$, also in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$. For a quantum statistical model, let $\mathcal A$ be a unital complex $C^*$-algebra: an associative complex algebra with nonzero identity $1$, a complete norm satisfying $\|AB\|\leq\|A\|\,\|B\|$, and a conjugate-linear involution $A\mapsto A^*$ satisfying $(A^*)^*=A$, $(AB)^*=B^*A^*$, and $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$. Its elements represent bounded observables. Let $\{\alpha_t:t\in\mathbb R\}$ be bijective complex-linear maps $\alpha_t:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ preserving multiplication and involution, with $\alpha_t(1)=1$, $\alpha_0=\operatorname{id}$, and $\alpha_{s+t}=\alpha_s\circ\alpha_t$; require $t\mapsto\alpha_t(A)$ to be norm-continuous for every $A\in\mathcal A$. A state is a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ with $\omega(1)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\geq0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$. For $b>0$ in the chosen flow-parameter units, define $S_b:=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\leq\operatorname{Im}z\leq b\}$. The state $\omega$ satisfies the KMS condition at width $b$ when for every $A,B\in\mathcal A$ there is a function $F_{A,B}:S_b\to\mathbb C$ with $\sup_{z\in S_b}|F_{A,B}(z)|<\infty$, continuous on $S_b$ and complex-differentiable at every point of its interior, such that

$$F_{A,B}(t)=\omega(A\alpha_t(B)),\qquad F_{A,B}(t+ib)=\omega(\alpha_t(B)A)\quad(t\in\mathbb R).$$

This all-observable boundary-value definition uses no separately declared analytic subalgebra. With the quantum statistical calibration $\beta_K=(k_BT_K)^{-1}$, a physical-time parameter $t$ in seconds has KMS width $b_t=\hbar\beta_K$ seconds. If the flow parameter is length $\lambda=ct$, use the reparameterized group $\widetilde\alpha_\lambda:=\alpha_{\lambda/c}$; its KMS width is $b_\lambda=c\hbar\beta_K$ metres. These are unit and parameter-convention assignments only. This definition introduces no Hilbert-space operator $H_K$ and does not identify the abstract automorphism flow or its strip width with the finite matter charge $H_\xi$ of [[lem-tgr-killing-energy-normalization]]. This item asserts neither the existence of an observable algebra or flow for a given thermodynamic-gravity model nor the existence of a KMS state or equilibrium.

On a specified smooth embedded null hypersurface $\mathcal H\subset M$,
write $i:\mathcal H\hookrightarrow M$ for the inclusion. A generator $\chi$
here is a smooth section of $i^*TM$ with $\chi_p\in T_p\mathcal H$
nonzero and null at each $p\in\mathcal H$. For a smooth tangent field $X$
on $\mathcal H$ and a smooth vector field $V$ along it, define
$\nabla_XV:=(i^*\nabla)_XV$ by [[def-pullback-connection]], applied to the
ambient tangent bundle and its metric-selected connection. The prescription
is independent of frames by
[[thm-pullback-connection-is-well-defined-and-functorial]]. In particular,
$\nabla_\chi\chi$ is a vector field along $\mathcal H$ and needs no chosen
ambient extension. If $\chi$ is the restriction of a smooth ambient field
$\widetilde\chi$, the same theorem gives
$\nabla_\chi\chi=(\nabla_{\widetilde\chi}\widetilde\chi)|_{\mathcal H}$;
thus this convention also covers the supplied ambient Killing generators.
The generator may admit a scalar $\kappa_{\rm geom}$ defined by
$\nabla_\chi\chi=\kappa_{\rm geom}\chi$. When the flow parameter has length units, $\kappa_{\rm geom}$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$; the corresponding acceleration-unit quantity $\kappa_{\rm acc}:=c^2\kappa_{\rm geom}$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. This definition does not assert a horizon exists, that $\kappa$ is constant, or that a temperature law follows. The formula $T_K=\hbar c\kappa_{\rm geom}/(2\pi k_B)$ requires a specified quantum/semiclassical model, and an area-entropy formula requires a separate thermodynamic identification. In particular, equal units do not identify local material entropy, finite statistical entropy, and area entropy, and no generalized second law is asserted here.

Let $O$ and the smooth fields $(g,\nabla,\xi,T,u,N_\xi,\beta)$ be as in
[[def-tgr-stationary-thermal-carriers]]. Then
$$\beta\text{ is Killing}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad N_\xi T=T_K\text{ for a constant }T_K>0.$$
When this holds, $\beta=\xi/(k_BT_K)$, and the Killing congruence has
$$\xi(N_\xi)=0,\qquad a=\nabla\log N_\xi,\qquad \theta=0,\qquad \sigma_{ab}=0.$$
If $\xi$ is replaced by $b\xi$ with a constant $b>0$, then
$N_\xi$ and $T_K$ scale by $b$, while $u$ and $\beta$ are unchanged.

Use the connected stationary thermal carrier of [[post-tgr-stationary-equilibrium]] on $O$. Let $N_\xi=\sqrt{-g(\xi,\xi)}>0$, $u=\xi/N_\xi$, and $\beta=u/(k_BT)$ as there, and assume the postulated Killing condition on $\beta$. Then a positive constant $T_K$ exists such that

$N_\xi(x)T(x)=T_K\quad\text{and}\quad \beta=\frac{\xi}{k_BT_K}\qquad(x\in O).$

In the same convention, $\xi(N_\xi)=0$, the observer acceleration satisfies $a=\nabla\log N_\xi$, the expansion and shear vanish, and

$\nabla\log T=-a.$

For any chosen reference event $x_{\rm ref}\in O$, $T_K=N_\xi(x_{\rm ref})T(x_{\rm ref})$. If the reference normalization has $N_\xi(x_{\rm ref})=1$, then $T_K$ is the local temperature at that event. Rescaling $\xi$ by a constant $b>0$ rescales $N_\xi$ and $T_K$ by $b$ while leaving the local scalar $T$ unchanged. The result is a conditional deduction from the selected physical postulate and the stated mathematical supplier; it is not a thermometer law for arbitrary observers or a KMS-existence theorem.

The real exponential function is $C^\infty$, and for every $m\in\mathbb N$,
$$\exp^{(m)}=\exp.$$
In particular $(\exp)'=\exp$.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Under the Countable Choice assumption [A4], the acceleration construction in [F1] uses the stated smooth future-directed timelike hyperbola and its actual tested field; the spectrum clause is conditional on the exact current batch-74 contour and exponential-current interfaces in [F1]. Applying [F2] to the rates from [A1] gives the stationary probability $p_*=1/(1+e^{2\pi cE/(a\hbar)})$, the Boltzmann ratio $p_*/(1-p_*)=e^{-E/(k_BT_{\rm eff})}$, and $T_{\rm eff}=\hbar a/(2\pi c k_B)$. The same supplier gives the stated $K_h/\mathsf T$ bound for every declared switch.

For $\rho>0$ define $\gamma_\rho(\tau)=(\rho\sinh(c\tau/\rho),\rho\cosh(c\tau/\rho),0,0)$. Differentiation using [F6] gives $\eta(\dot\gamma_\rho,\dot\gamma_\rho)=-c^2$ and $\eta(\ddot\gamma_\rho,\ddot\gamma_\rho)=c^4/\rho^2$, so the curve is future timelike, parametrized by proper seconds, with acceleration magnitude $c^2/\rho$. The field $\chi_\kappa$ has norm $-\kappa^2\rho^2$, hence $N=\kappa\rho$. Substituting $a=c^2/\rho$ into step 1.1 yields $T_U(\rho)=\hbar c/(2\pi k_B\rho)=T_K^{\rm acc}/N$ with the stated reference normalization.

In the flat length-coordinate chart, $\chi^0=\kappa x^1$ and $\chi^1=\kappa x^0$. Thus $(\nabla_\chi\chi)^0=\kappa^2x^0$ and $(\nabla_\chi\chi)^1=\kappa^2x^1$. On $x^0=x^1>0$ this equals $\kappa\chi$, verifying the claimed surface-gravity coefficient under [F3]. Replacing $\chi$ by $b\chi$ multiplies $\kappa,N,T_K^{\rm acc}$ by $b$, so their ratio at every fixed orbit is unchanged.

Under the additional bath and reference-match assumptions [A2]–[A3], its lapse is the $N$ of step 2.1 because its Killing field is $\chi_\kappa$. Then [F4]–[F5] give the bath temperature $T_{\rm bath}(\rho)=T_K^{\rm bath}/N(\rho)$ and $T_K^{\rm bath}=T_{\rm bath}(\rho_0)=T_U(\rho_0)=T_K^{\rm acc}$. Therefore $T_{\rm bath}(\rho)=T_U(\rho)$ throughout the connected wedge. This is the explicitly assumed comparison of two model constructions.

citations.quote:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as defined in [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the massless acceleration branch of [[post-tgr-exponential-current-and-spectral-thermometer]] with proper acceleration $a>0$ in metres per square second, gap $E>0$ in joules, $c>0$ in metres per second, $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds, $k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin, and $\gamma_{\rm acc}>0$ in square metres per square second. The adopted rates are $r_\uparrow=\gamma_{\rm acc}S_a(E/\hbar)$ and $r_\downarrow=\gamma_{\rm acc}S_a(-E/\hbar)$. The unique stationary excited-state probability of the defined two-state model and its effective temperature are

$$p_* = \frac{1}{1+e^{2\pi cE/(a\hbar)}},\qquad T_{\rm eff}=\frac{\hbar a}{2\pi c k_B}.$$

For any nonzero real $h\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$ and switching duration $\mathsf T>0$ seconds, let $Q_{\mathsf T}^{(a)}(\nu)=R_{\mathsf T}^{(C_a)}(\nu)/(\mathsf T\|h\|_2^2)$ and $K_h=(2\pi\|h\|_2^2)^{-1}\int_\mathbb R|z||\widehat h(z)|^2dz$, with the definitions in [[lem-tgr-spectral-thermometer]]. Then the leading switched coefficient obeys $|Q_{\mathsf T}^{(a)}(\nu)-S_a(\nu)|\le\operatorname{Lip}(S_a)K_h/\mathsf T$. This is a coefficient estimate and does not assert an all-order transition probability.

On the Minkowski right Rindler wedge $W_R=\{(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3):x^1>|x^0|\}$, use length coordinates $x^0=ct$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $\rho=\sqrt{(x^1)^2-(x^0)^2}>0$, and the boost Killing field $\chi_\kappa=\kappa(x^1\partial_{x^0}+x^0\partial_{x^1})$ with $\kappa>0$ in inverse metres. Its lapse is $N=\sqrt{-\eta(\chi_\kappa,\chi_\kappa)}=\kappa\rho$. The orbit at fixed $\rho$ has proper acceleration $a(\rho)=c^2/\rho$, so the effective model temperature there is $T_U(\rho)=\hbar c/(2\pi k_B\rho)$. With reference event on $\rho_0=\kappa^{-1}$, $N(\rho_0)=1$ and $T_K^{\rm acc}:=T_U(\rho_0)=\hbar c\kappa/(2\pi k_B)$, hence $T_U(\rho)=T_K^{\rm acc}/N(\rho)$. On the future Rindler horizon $x^0=x^1>0$, direct differentiation gives $\nabla_{\chi_\kappa}\chi_\kappa=\kappa\chi_\kappa$, so the generator's $\kappa_{\rm geom}$ is $\kappa$ under the definition of [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. Rescaling $\chi_\kappa$ by $b>0$ rescales $N$ and $T_K^{\rm acc}$ by $b$ while leaving the proper model temperature unchanged.

If a selected stationary bath of [[post-tgr-stationary-equilibrium]] is additionally adopted on $W_R$ with its selected Killing field identified with this same $\chi_\kappa$, and its reference proper temperature is identified with $T_U(\rho_0)$, then the bath's local proper temperature agrees with $T_U(\rho)$ by [[pthm-tgr-tolman-ehrenfest]]. Both identifications are extra model assumptions. No general Unruh-state, KMS, horizon-formation, Hawking-radiation, or empirical thermometer claim follows.

derivations.claim: Under the Countable Choice assumption [A2], apply [F1] first at acceleration $a$ and then at $2a$. The fixed positive constants cancel in the ratio, so $T_U(2a)/T_U(a)=2$.

On a fixed boost congruence, $\rho_a=c^2/a$ and $\rho_{2a}=c^2/(2a)=\rho_a/2$, hence $N_{2a}=\kappa\rho_{2a}=N_a/2$. Substitution into [F1] gives the same ratio of effective temperatures and the common reference $T_K^{\rm acc}$.

Under $\chi_\kappa\mapsto b\chi_\kappa$ with $b>0$, [F1] gives $N\mapsto bN$ and $T_K^{\rm acc}\mapsto bT_K^{\rm acc}$ at each orbit; therefore $T_K^{\rm acc}/N$ and each effective local temperature are unchanged. The comparison is entirely conditional on [F1]'s model assumptions.
